|strategy=By [mailto:zube@eagle.cc.ukans.edu Nick Zube]<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/ajedisconcentration.html</ref>

Sometimes, you just want a little insurance. And this nifty Interrupt is like a double-breasted, gilt-edged, full-coverage package for some embarrassing situations.

As a Used Interrupt, [[A Jedi's Concentration]] is the perfect bodyguard: play it to prevent anyone from being targeted by lightsabers for the remainder of a battle &#150; as long as you've got someone with a lightsaber there, too. While this locks your lightsabers out of the battle, too, sometimes, the trade-off is worth it. Imagine that your fledgling main squad of EPP [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], and [[Chewie (The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game){{!}}Chewie]] is ambushed by [[Darth Vader]], his buddy [[Darth Maul]], and their girlfriend, [[Mara Jade]] &#150; all armed with lightsabers. Keeping [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]] and [[Chewie (The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game){{!}}Chewie]] (and their high forfeit values) alive is more important than a shaky swing at any of the Dark Side characters.

[[A Jedi's Concentration]] is also a great way to give a duel-happy opponent pause. Lose this Interrupt, and your opponent must either cancel the duel or lose a whopping 4 Force! While duels may have been few and far between, expect the scene to heat up with the introduction of [[Darth Maul]], who absolutely hates concentrating Jedi &#150; they make him lose 5 Force to initiate his duel instead of one!

Use [[A Jedi's Concentration]] against [[Darth Maul]] to both protect his saber and save [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] from his duel.

Your opponent's initiating a duel. Every turn. Make him pay. Big-time.
